versions.notes:
**New**

- **Update MUGIC's firmware over Wi-Fi**, no cable needed. When a newer firmware is available, choose
  **Update over Wi-Fi**: the wizard downloads it at once, then installs it as soon as MUGIC is on Wi-Fi
  (your network or MUGIC's own), in about a minute, and checks that MUGIC comes back. If anything goes
  wrong, MUGIC keeps the firmware it has. A USB cable still works too (**Use a USB cable instead**).
- The firmware page lists what's new in every version since the one your MUGIC runs, in a box you can
  scroll.

**Fixed**

- With several MUGICs nearby, the list on the first page no longer keeps reordering itself: each MUGIC
  keeps its place, and new ones are added at the bottom. The signal strength (Strong, Good, Weak) no
  longer flickers either.
- Updating over Wi-Fi: the progress no longer sits at 100% with nothing happening. Once the firmware has
  left this computer, the page shows how long MUGIC has been installing it, and the wizard checks MUGIC's
  version itself, so it reports success even if MUGIC restarts into the new firmware before answering
  (it used to stay on "Sending" after a successful update).
- Updating over Wi-Fi on a Mac: the wizard now asks for the Local Network permission it needs to reach
  MUGIC. Without it the update could fail at once, and the wizard then wrongly said MUGIC ran the new
  firmware. It now reports success only once MUGIC itself names the new version, and says so when it
  couldn't reach MUGIC or MUGIC came back on its old firmware.
- With firmware older than 2.3.0, which can't report its version, the list of what's new now says why it
  starts at the very first version.
- After an update on MUGIC's own network, the wizard asks you to rejoin that network (MUGIC's restart
  makes this computer leave it), so it can see that MUGIC is back.
- The last page no longer says "receiving MUGIC's data" with frozen numbers once the data has stopped:
  after 3 s it says so, in blue, and why when this computer has left MUGIC's network.

**New**

- **Works with MUGIC MOTION Plugin 2.10.0.** The plug-in's **Set up with MUGIC Wizard** pauses the plug-in while the Wizard runs. Choosing **MUGIC MOTION Plugin** at the end launches it and closes the Wizard, and the Wizard hands the setup (Bluetooth name or Wi-Fi port) back to the plug-in, which switches over by itself.
- **Messages front and center.** They appear right under the page's text in a colour-blind-safe box, the same as in the plug-in, each with a mark: **!** something's wrong, **→** your turn (a wait shows ". . ."), **✓** it worked. MUGIC's light colours are unchanged.
- "Ready to set up" shows a progress bar and the seconds left while MUGIC restarts and joins the network.
- "MUGIC is working" shows the live motion in a green box, with what yaw, pitch and roll mean.
- With USB, the Wizard explains that only one app at a time can use MUGIC's port (**Disconnect the wizard from the port**).
- Each choice under "Where do you want to use MUGIC?" has an (i) saying what it does; the first is now **MUGIC MOTION Plugin**.
- **Menu → Help** ("MUGIC® Wizard: how it works"): modes, buttons, light colours, common problems, Contact support, and **Show log file** / **Clear log**. Also **Start over** and the Wizard's version.
- The top of each page says "Your MUGIC name is: …", in larger type.

**Fixed**

- The Wizard said MUGIC's light turns yellow on its own network; it turns blue.

**Fixed**

- The wizard could quit on the "Which Wi-Fi network?" page when MUGIC finished listing the
  networks it sees.

**New**

- **Switch modes without setting up again.** On the "How should MUGIC send its data?" page, a mode
  MUGIC already has settings for offers **Switch to this mode** (no typing: it uses the saved
  network and password, then checks that data arrives) or **Reconfigure**. A mode never set up
  offers **Configure new mode**. The current mode offers **Check it works**.
  For your network, the card shows the saved network's name (**Switch to 'HomeNet'**) and warns
  when this computer is on a different network, making **Reconfigure** the main button.
- **USB is checked too.** After switching MUGIC to USB, the wizard reads its data over the cable and
  shows live motion, like the other modes. A cable that only charges is caught: the wizard says to
  use a data cable. For Max and other apps, it names MUGIC's USB port and speed (74880 baud).
- **MUGIC's colours.** Each mode shows the colour of MUGIC's light: purple for your network, blue
  for MUGIC's own network, green for Bluetooth, yellow for USB.
- **Without the app: using MUGIC's buttons** explains how to change modes with the Mode and
  Power buttons, and what each light colour means.

**Improved**

- **The network list stays.** Going back after a failed try shows the Wi-Fi networks again, with
  your last choice selected, instead of an empty box. If MUGIC can't be reached, the wizard asks you
  to press **Power + Mode** and refreshes the list by itself; **Refresh list** scans again.
- **This computer's networks too.** The list adds the networks this computer sees, and marks
  5 GHz-only ones "MUGIC can't use it" (MUGIC needs 2.4 GHz), so a 5 GHz network can't be picked by
  mistake.
- **Typing suggests.** Typing a network name filters the list as you type; click a match to use it.
- **Always a next step.** When setup fails, the main button says what to do: **Try again: choose the
  network**, **Re-enter the password**, or **Use MUGIC's own network**, with the likely cause in plain
  words. While MUGIC joins, the wizard says what its light means: purple joined, yellow didn't.
- **Advanced settings say what to do.** When MUGIC can't be reached (for example after switching it
  to USB, which turns Bluetooth off), a big box asks you to press **Power + Mode** instead of a small
  line at the bottom; the settings appear as soon as MUGIC answers.
- **Waiting shows.** Scans and other waits show dots that grow every second.
- **Easier to read.** Text grows as you enlarge the window, and grey text is brighter.
- **USB cable tips.** After a firmware update the wizard says to unplug the cable and turn MUGIC on;
  when MUGIC doesn't show up, it explains that a MUGIC turned off while plugged in only charges.
- The **Main Menu** button is now just **Menu** (Show log file / Clear log): nothing there is part
  of the setup.

**New**

- **MUGIC Wizard** sets up your MUGIC step by step over Bluetooth: no web page, no typing an IP
  address. Turn your MUGIC on, press **Power + Mode**, and pick it from the list.
- **Firmware check.** The wizard tells you when your MUGIC's firmware is out of date and opens the
  update page for you.
- **Choose how MUGIC sends its data:** Wi-Fi on your network, Wi-Fi on MUGIC's own network,
  Bluetooth, or USB cable.
- **Your network, filled in.** The wizard knows which Wi-Fi network this computer is on, lists the
  networks your MUGIC can see, and can use the password already saved on this computer, so you
  rarely type anything. It sets this computer as the destination automatically.
- **Checked, not guessed.** The wizard waits until data actually arrives on this computer, and when
  something goes wrong it says what: wrong password, network not found, or a network that blocks
  devices from talking to each other (common at schools, offices and on guest Wi-Fi).
- **Advanced** settings for ports and other computers MUGIC also sends to.
- **Main Menu → Show log file / Clear log** for troubleshooting.
- Works best with MUGIC firmware 2.3.0 or later; older firmware works with fewer features.
